listenings.text: Thank you all for joining this briefing. Let me walk you through the format, in three parts. First, the opening. Each panelist has three minutes, no slides. Second, the discussion. I will ask each of you one question, and then I will open the floor. Please keep your answers to about two minutes, so everyone gets the same airtime. Third, the closing round. I will ask each of you for one final sentence, a soundbite that the audience can take home. One more thing: some questions from the floor may be off-topic. If that happens, feel free to answer briefly and pivot back to the theme of the panel. To recap: three minutes to open, two minutes per answer, one sentence to close.

I was on this panel two years ago, so let me share what I learned. What surprised me most was not the questions from the moderator. It was the questions from the floor. Somebody always asks a curveball, usually about politics. My advice is simple. Do not try to answer everything. It is usually better to give a short, honest answer and then build on something another panelist said. As one of my colleagues likes to say, the audience remembers your attitude, not your grammar. And prepare your final sentence in advance. Admittedly, it feels a bit artificial, but it is the sentence people will quote on social media the next day.
